Hikes & wild water

Choose the right edge

Ruta del Cares

22–24 km

Return from Poncebos to Caín · 6–8 hours · moderate overall, but exposed cliff-edge sections.

  • Fit teens/adults
  • No services on trail
  • Not for vertigo
  • Arrive early for summer parking
Trail source ↗

Ruta del Alba

14 km

Return from Soto de Agües · about 4 hours · easy, family-friendly route into the Llaímo gorge.

  • First 4.5–5 km gentle/paved
  • Rockier final gorge
  • Good mixed-ability choice
Trail source ↗

Bulnes on foot

1.5–2 h

Each way on the Canal del Tejo path from Poncebos—or take the tunnel funicular.

  • No road reaches the village
  • Funicular takes about 7 min
  • Jun–Sep: reported 10:00–20:00
  • 2026 fares: €22.16 return; recheck
Funicular source ↗

Covadonga Lakes

Easy loops

Short glacial-lake walks with minimal ascent; there is little shade.

  • All ages with basic mobility
  • Bring water and sun protection
  • Use the peak-season shuttle
Official guide ↗
Food & cider

Order Asturias first

Start with the food that belongs here, then widen the table.

The ritual

Let the cider breathe.

Natural sidra is still and unfiltered. The high pour—escanciado—aerates a small measure called a culín. Drink it as if it were a shot, whilst it's still fresh

Distinctly Asturian

Prioritise these local classics.

Common here, broadly Spanish

Easy to find, but not uniquely Asturian. “Wine” is already English; ask for vino in Spanish.

From elsewhere in Spain

Good food, different regional origin: order knowingly.

Your travel window

Four dates to circle

2027 programmes were not yet published when researched on 25 September 2026. Dates below are derived from official recurrence rules or normal annual patterns and must be rechecked in spring 2027.

25 Jul*Rule-derived

Fiesta del Vaquero

Braña de Aristébano · last Sunday of July. Traditional vaqueiro wedding reenactment.

25 Jul†Usual annual date

Fiesta del Pastor

Vega de Enol at the Covadonga Lakes · shepherds’ festival, usually 25 July.

1 Aug*Rule-derived

Día de Asturias

Gijón · first Sunday of August, with folklore, bagpipes and traditional dress.

See the Gijón day plan →
7 Aug*Rule-derived

Descenso del Sella

Arriondas → Ribadesella · 20 km canoe race, noon start. It coincides with the final trip day; book early.

Also watch for Festival del Bollu in Arriondas around 30 Jul–1 Aug (pattern only), and the possible start of Gijón’s Semana Grande near the trip’s end. Sella source ↗ · Día de Asturias source ↗

Practical Asturias

Make the logistics disappear

Open the panels you need. Prices and transport frequencies were recorded in September 2026 and should be checked before July 2027.

Where to base
  • Oviedo: transport hub, museums, architecture, cider evenings.
  • Gijón: urban beach and strong central-coast position.
  • Avilés: compact historic centre, quick airport access and an easy launch point for Salinas, Cudillero and the western coast.

A two-base trip works well: choose Oviedo, Gijón or Avilés for the central/western half, then move east.

Useful apps
  • ALSA: bus tickets, schedules and regional tracking.
  • Alsa Mobi4U: journey planner with live information.
  • CTA CONECTA: official regional transport planner; mixed reviews, so treat as backup.
  • Renfe: trains. Moovit: useful around Oviedo.
  • Ride-hailing: Freenow, Cabify and PideTaxi are alternatives to Uber.
ALSA app ↗
Weather & what to pack

Expect mild Atlantic summer conditions rather than Mediterranean heat: roughly 20–25°C by day, 15–16°C at night and sea around 21°C. Rain and mist remain possible.

  • Pack a light waterproof and warm layer.
  • Use grippy footwear for wet stone and trails.
  • Carry sun protection for the exposed Covadonga lakes.

These figures are approximate and partly use an Atlantic-coast proxy; check a current local forecast before each outing.

Eating hours & etiquette
  • Lunch commonly 13:30–15:30; dinner 21:00–midnight.
  • Kitchens may close between services.
  • The bill is not brought unprompted: say la cuenta, por favor.
  • Tipping is optional; round up or leave €1–2 for good service, up to about 10% at fine dining.
  • Sobremesa—lingering after a meal—is normal.
  • At Covadonga, remember it is an active sanctuary.
Shoe shopping

Oviedo: Calle Uría, Caveda, Posada Herrera and the old town. Verified store leads include Lotusse at Calle Posada Herrera 2, Calzados Firenze and Mondo Zapatos.

Gijón: Calle Corrida. El Corte Inglés offers several Spanish brands.

Small shops may close around 13:30/14:00–16:30 and on Sundays.

Hour by hour

The plan

09:00

Bus from Avilés to Covadonga

10:30

Santa Cueva & Basilica

The cave chapel of the Santina above its waterfall, then the pink basilica. It is an active pilgrimage site — dress respectfully and expect masses through the morning.

11:15

Shuttle up to the lakes

In high summer private cars cannot continue past Covadonga: the Plan de Acceso runs shuttle buses from Cangas de Onís station and the P2–P4 car parks up to the lakes. Buy tickets online in advance.

11:45

Lakes of Enol & Ercina

Since there is almost no shade, bring hats, water, sunscreen. Bocadillos (sandwiches with baguette bread) will be prepared for lunch.

15:45

Bus to Llanes

19:15

Early dinner in Llanes

20:30

Bus back to Avilés

The last leg

OVD airport to Avilés

~20 min

ALSA airport bus

The cheapest and simplest choice. Direct buses run every 30 minutes to Avilés bus station and cost approximately €4.50 per person.

Check ALSA tickets ↗
13–17 min

Taxi

The taxi rank is right outside the terminal. Expect to pay roughly €25–30 for the journey to Avilés.

You can also contact Radio Taxi Villa del Adelantado ↗. You may need to communicate in Spanish; a translation app can help.

~13 min

Rental car

A quick drive into Avilés, and a practical choice if you are picking up a car to explore Asturias.

Getting around

Why rent a car?

Follow the green landscapes

Driving is one of the best ways to see Asturias beyond the main towns — a car makes it easier to reach coastal villages, beaches and mountain scenery.

Explore Spain at your own pace

Outside of Asturias, much of the landscape becomes more dry and flat rather than green and mountainous.

Plan a flexible drop-off

You can generally collect a rental car at one Spanish airport, town or city and return it at another; confirm the drop-off location when picking up your rental car.

No car? Buses still work

ALSA links the cities and the airport, and Renfe covers trains — see the practical panels for the useful apps.
